bull.b: Revenue growth alongside a richer product mix is a constructive sign for the business model: Q2 sales rose 6.9% and gross margin reached 37.4%. Greater acceptance of higher-end T-Rex and Balance products can support pricing, mix quality, and more durable revenue growth.

An exclusive three-year global HYROX partnership broadens Zepp’s route to customers and embeds Amazfit across training, competition, recovery, and connected apps. The hardware, software, and performance-data integration can deepen ecosystem engagement and strengthen brand differentiation over the coming quarters.

Retiring US$46.7 million of debt since the beginning of 2023 is a tangible balance-sheet improvement. Lower debt can reduce future financing demands and improve financial flexibility, giving management more room to fund product investment while pursuing its stated profitable-growth path.

bear.b: Profitability remains unproven despite revenue recovery: Q2 net loss widened to US$11.3 million as foreign-exchange headwinds and higher research, marketing, and brand-building spending weighed on results. Persistent losses could restrict internally funded investment and delay a durable earnings recovery.

Cash generation is not yet dependable: operating and free cash flow were negative in both 2024 and 2025. This means the company has not consistently funded operations internally, increasing reliance on cash reserves or balance-sheet support if losses continue over the next several quarters.

Debt-to-equity reached about 1.06 in 2025, up from a lower leverage profile in 2020–2023, while ROE has remained negative since 2022. Rising leverage alongside losses reduces financial flexibility and leaves less capacity to absorb setbacks or finance growth without added funding pressure.
